title: Kinetic admission pacer: continuous intake shaping and kernel-aware pacing
creator: Jonah Kim
description:
Goal: reduce 99th/99.9th prefill+decode latency spikes during bursty ingress by introducing a token-rate admission pacer that shapes incoming requests with kernel-awareness and attention-mode hints. The pacer should operate continuously (not epoch-based) and integrate with existing admission and batch-shaper components rather than replacing them.

Motivation: we still see transient tail spikes when many short prefill-heavy requests collide with long decode streams. Existing admission heuristics react too late or oscillate when kernel selection choices cause step changes in decode throughput. A pacing layer that smooths arrival rates while signalling preferred kernel/attention modes to scheduler should reduce kernel churn, improve batching efficiency, and lower tail percentiles without materially degrading median latency for most customers.
design_notes:
Core ideas: 1) Per-route lightweight token-leaky-bucket that emits per-request pacing tokens and a suggested kernel affinity label (e.g., "cuda-fp16-compact" vs "int8-wrapped"). 2) A kernel-cost estimator informed by recent kernel latency distributions per seq_len/model_variant. 3) Continuous admission that adjusts leak rate by observed queue depth and SLO headroom, with reactive short-term bursts allowed for VIPs. 4) Attention-mode hints: for models with FlashAttention or grouped attention optimizations, hint 'attention-mode: grouped' to encourage scheduler packing compatible kernels. 5) Hedge policy: when estimated tail risk exceeds threshold, proactively reserve a small decode pool and route high-risk inferences to it (fast-fallthrough).

Trade-offs considered: we can either bias pacing to protect tail (higher median increase) or bias to preserve median (less tail benefit). Initial shaper will target 5-10% median latency increase cap while aiming for >=30% reduction in 99.9th for benchmark traffic. Pacer must be stateless across infra restarts (avoid persistent tokens) and work in both Hosted and Dedicated modes.

API/Config: per-route config: paced: true/false; base_tokens_per_sec; burst_ratio; vip_weight; kernel_affinity_policy: [preferred, allowed]; attention_hint: [auto, grouped, standard].
tasks: Spike: offline simulator to model token-pacer + kernel-aware scheduler (3d) - outputs: perf matrix and microbench scripts
Implement lightweight per-route token bucket and admission hook (ENG) (5d)
Integrate kernel-cost estimator using recent kernel timing histograms (2d)
Add attention-mode hint plumbing from API layer through scheduler (2d)
Create hedging pool and fast-fallthrough logic (3d)
End-to-end integration tests with synthetic microbursts and long-decoder workloads (3d)
Canary rollout: 5% traffic hosted, smoke dashboards, automatic rollback (1d)
Performance run vs baseline (latency percentiles, throughput, cost delta) (2d)
Docs: console config UI, default safe settings, and runbook (2d)
acceptance_criteria: 99.9th prefill+decode latency reduced by >=30% on synthetic burst test under configuration that keeps median increase <=10%
No regressions in throughput for long-decode steady streams (within 5%)
Config knobs available per-route and editable via Console
Canary run shows stable kernel selection (no >10% oscillation per minute) and no production incidents during 72h window
E2E tests cover both attention-mode hints and kernel-affinity changes
